sunday.themeNote: All three readings this week circle around one big idea: God places authority in specific people and trusts them to carry it well. In Isaiah, God hands a key to a faithful servant. In the Gospel, Jesus hands that same kind of key to Peter and builds his whole Church on Peter's trust. Paul reminds us that behind all of this is a God whose wisdom is far beyond what any of us can fully map out, and who deserves our awe and gratitude.

readings.label: First Reading
readings.fullText:
Thus says the LORD to Shebna, master of the palace:
"I will thrust you from your office
and pull you down from your station.
On that day I will summon my servant
Eliakim, son of Hilkiah;
I will clothe him with your robe,
and gird him with your sash,
and give over to him your authority.
He shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
and to the house of Judah.
I will place the key of the House of David on Eliakim's shoulder;
when he opens, no one shall shut,
when he shuts, no one shall open.
I will fix him like a peg in a sure spot,
to be a place of honor for his family."
readings.summary: God is speaking through the prophet Isaiah, and he is making a leadership change. A man named Shebna has been in charge, but God is removing him and putting a man named Eliakim in his place. God describes giving Eliakim a special key, one that lets him open doors no one else can close and close doors no one else can open. This key is a sign of real, lasting authority given by God himself.

reflection.reflection: God sometimes moves trusted people into new roles not as a punishment to others but as a gift to everyone. Being chosen for something important is also being called to serve.
reflection.question: Think of someone in your life who leads quietly and without much fanfare. What do you think makes their kind of leadership feel trustworthy?

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.fullText:
R. (8bc) Lord, your love is eternal; do not forsake the work of your hands.
I will give thanks to you, O LORD, with all my heart,
for you have heard the words of my mouth;
in the presence of the angels I will sing your praise;
I will worship at your holy temple.
R. Lord, your love is eternal; do not forsake the work of your hands.
I will give thanks to your name,
because of your kindness and your truth:
When I called, you answered me;
you built up strength within me.
R. Lord, your love is eternal; do not forsake the work of your hands.
The LORD is exalted, yet the lowly he sees,
and the proud he knows from afar.
Your kindness, O LORD, endures forever;
forsake not the work of your hands.
R. Lord, your love is eternal; do not forsake the work of your hands.
readings.summary: The psalm is a song of gratitude from someone who prayed and felt God come through for them. The writer praises God openly, even in front of others, because God answered when called. The psalm holds two ideas together: God is great and far above us, and yet God still notices the humble and the overlooked. The repeated refrain asks God not to walk away from the people he has made.

reflection.reflection: God hears us when we call out, and that is worth saying out loud. Gratitude shared openly can itself become a kind of prayer.
reflection.question: Is there something that worked out recently, big or small, that you have not really stopped to feel grateful for yet?

readings.label: Second Reading
readings.fullText:
Oh, the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God!
How inscrutable are his judgments and how unsearchable his ways!
For who has known the mind of the Lord
or who has been his counselor?
Or who has given the Lord anything
that he may be repaid?
For from him and through him and for him are all things.
To him be glory forever. Amen.
readings.summary: Paul is not explaining a doctrine here so much as standing in wonder. He is saying that God's wisdom and knowledge are so deep that no human being could ever fully understand them. No one taught God anything, and no one has ever done God a favor that needed paying back. Everything comes from God, exists through God, and finds its purpose in God.

reflection.reflection: Paul is not frustrated by how much he does not know about God. He is amazed by it. There is an invitation here to let mystery feel like wonder instead of a problem to solve.
reflection.question: When something in your life does not make sense right now, does it feel more like a locked door or more like a question you are still sitting with?

readings.label: Gospel
readings.fullText:
Jesus went into the region of Caesarea Philippi and
he asked his disciples,
"Who do people say that the Son of Man is?"
They replied, "Some say John the Baptist, others Elijah,
still others Jeremiah or one of the prophets."
He said to them, "But who do you say that I am?"
Simon Peter said in reply,
"You are the Christ, the Son of the living God."
Jesus said to him in reply,
"Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah.
For flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my heavenly Father.
And so I say to you, you are Peter,
and upon this rock I will build my church,
and the gates of the netherworld shall not prevail against it.
I will give you the keys to the kingdom of heaven.
Whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven;
and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven."
Then he strictly ordered his disciples
to tell no one that he was the Christ.
readings.summary: Jesus asks his disciples a direct question: who do people think he is? He gets a few different answers. Then he makes it personal and asks who they think he is. Peter speaks up and says Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of the living God. Jesus tells Peter that this answer did not come from human reasoning but from God. He then gives Peter a new name and says he will build his Church on him, handing him the keys to the kingdom.

reflection.reflection: Jesus does not just ask about opinions. He asks what you personally think of him. That question is still open, and there is no wrong way to be honest about where you are.
reflection.question: If Jesus asked you today, right now, who you think he is, what would you actually say?
